facts.statement: Fossils of the type species Baptornis advenus were found in Kansas, an area covered by the shallow Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The fossils of Baptornis advenus, the type species, were discovered in Kansas, which at its time was mostly covered by the Western Interior Seaway, a shallow shelf sea.

facts.statement: Baptornis is also known from Sweden and possibly occurred throughout the Holarctic region.
facts.quote: It is now known to have also occurred in today's Sweden, where the Turgai Strait joined the ancient North Sea; possibly, it occurred in the entire Holarctic.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh discovered the first fossils of Baptornis in the 1870s.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh discovered the first fossils of this bird in the 1870s.

facts.statement: Baptornis was one of the first Mesozoic birds known to science, alongside Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: This was, alongside the Archaeopteryx, one of the first Mesozoic birds to become known to science.

facts.statement: Baptornis was loon-sized with a markedly elongated neck compared to its relatives.
facts.quote: The loon-sized bird was of middle size among its relatives and had a markedly elongated neck.

facts.statement: Baptornis held prey in its beak like mergansers rather than spearing it like darters.
facts.quote: Unlike a darter however, it could not spear its prey, but instead held it with its beak like today's mergansers.

facts.statement: Coprolites associated with Baptornis contain remains of the sabre-toothed fish Enchodus.
facts.quote: Specimen UNSM 20030 was found associated with some coprolites. These are small round lumps - maybe a centimeter in diameter or so - and contain the remains of a small species of the sabre-toothed "herring" Enchodus, possibly E. parvus.

facts.statement: Baptornis provides the only certain record of food for the Hesperornithes group.
facts.quote: The only certain record of Hesperornithes' food found so far comes from Baptornis

facts.statement: Baptornis was excellently adapted for swimming and diving but thought to be clumsy on land.
facts.quote: While it was excellently adapted to swimming and diving, Baptornis is thought to have been clumsy on land, pushing itself along the rocks with its feet rather than actually walking.

facts.statement: Baptornis had lower legs flush against its body with feet stretched sideways, making it unable to stand upright.
facts.quote: The natural position of the lower legs was flush against the body, with the feet stretched out sideways and thus it would have been unable to move upright without toppling over.

facts.statement: The family Baptornithidae was established for Baptornis due to its peculiar characteristics among Hesperornithes.
facts.quote: As Baptornis was quite peculiar among the Hesperornithes, the family Baptornithidae has been established for it.

facts.statement: Parascaniornis stensioi, previously thought to be a flamingo or loon, is now considered to belong with Baptornis.
facts.quote: However, it was recently established that the supposed "Cretaceous flamingo" Parascaniornis stensioi from the Late Cretaceous of Ivö Island in Sweden was not a flamingo and neither, as suggested by others, a gaviiform (loon) nor a procellariiform, but in fact belongs with Baptornis.

facts.statement: The classification of Neogaeornis is debated; it might be a baptornithid or related to modern Gaviiformes or Procellariiformes.
facts.quote: More interesting - or controversial - is the case of Neogaeornis. This bird, whose remains were found in Chile, might be a baptornithid also. Others consider it closely related to certain modern birds, either the Gaviiformes, or the Procellariiformes.

facts.statement: Baptornis was a genus of aquatic birds that lived in the Late Cretaceous, about 83 to 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Baptornis ("ave buceadora") es un género de aves subacuáticas que vivieron en el Cretácico tardío, hace unos 83-80 millones de años.

facts.statement: Baptornis weighed about 7 kg and measured 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: Pesaba unos 7kg y medía 1m.

facts.statement: No complete skeletons of Baptornis have been found, so the skeleton of its relative Hesperornis was used for reconstruction.
facts.quote: Nunca se ha encontrado un esqueleto completo, por lo que para la reconstrucción de su esqueleto se ha utilizado el esqueleto de un primo cercano, Hesperornis, para reconstruir partes que faltaban.

facts.statement: Baptornis had an unusually long neck that allowed it to strike fish with its sharp beak.
facts.quote: Eran aves que tenían un cuello inusualmente largo, lo que le habría permitido arrojarse con su afilado pico contra los peces.

facts.statement: Unlike modern birds, Baptornis had small sharp teeth covering its jaws.
facts.quote: A diferencia de las aves modernas las mandíbulas de las aves del género Baptornis estaban cubiertas de pequeños dientes afilados.

facts.statement: The sharp teeth were useful for holding fish firmly, which made up most of its diet.
facts.quote: Estos dientes eran muy útiles para sujetar firmemente los peces, que constituían la mayor parte de su dieta.

facts.statement: Baptornis was likely constantly threatened by large marine reptiles like mosasaurs living beneath the sea surface.
facts.quote: Todas estas aves debían de estar amenazadas constantemente por los grandes reptiles marinos, como los mosasaurios, que vivían bajo la superficie del mar.

facts.statement: Baptornis were excellent swimmers that used their huge webbed feet for propulsion, as their tiny wings were useless.
facts.quote: Las aves del género Baptornis eran unas magníficas nadadoras. Nadaban utilizando sus enormes pies palmeados, puesto que sus minúsculas alas no le servían.

facts.statement: Baptornis were skilled underwater predators capable of maneuvering well by twisting and turning quickly while chasing prey.
facts.quote: Eran unas depredadoras subacuáticas muy hábiles, podían maniobrar muy bien, revolviéndose y girando rápidamente mientras perseguían a su presa.

facts.statement: Baptornis had a torpedo-like profile and were aerodynamic, facilitating their movements in water.
facts.quote: Todo su cuerpo estaba especialmente diseñado para sumergirse. Tenían el perfil de un torpedo y eran aereodinámicas, lo que le facilitaba mucho sus movimientos en el agua.

facts.statement: Baptornis's tiny wings only served to propel them forward while swimming.
facts.quote: Sus alas tan minúsculas solo les servían para impulsarse hacia delante mientras nadaban.

facts.statement: The flat sternum of Baptornis indicates that the muscles controlling its wings were small and weak.
facts.quote: Además, la forma plana de su esternón demuestra que los músculos que accionaban las alas eran pequeños y débiles.

facts.statement: Baptornis had huge webbed feet that provided almost all the propulsive force when diving or swimming.
facts.quote: Las aves del género Baptornis tenían unos enormes pies palmeados que le proporcionaban caso toda la fuerza de propulsión cuando buceaban o nadaban.

facts.statement: Baptornis birds likely found walking on land difficult because their legs were positioned far behind their bodies.
facts.quote: A las aves del género Baptornis les habría costado mucho caminar sobre tierra debido a que sus patas estaban colocadas muy atrás del cuerpo.

facts.statement: Baptornis probably spent most of its life swimming in water or floating on the sea.
facts.quote: Seguramente pasaba la mayor parte de su vida dentro del agua o flotando sobre el mar.

facts.statement: Fossils of Baptornis are found in limestone rocks that typically form at shorelines, indicating a coastal habitat.
facts.quote: Esto nos lo indica también que los fósiles de las aves del género Baptornis se han encontrado en rocas de tipo calizo, que normalmente se forman en las orillas.

facts.statement: Baptornis likely spent most of its life in open sea and only went to land to lay eggs and raise its young.
facts.quote: Esto da la idea de que las aves del género Baptornis pasaban la mayor parte de su vida en mar abierto y que solo iban a tierra para poner huevos y criar a sus pequeños.

facts.statement: The genus Baptornis belongs to the parent group Baptornithidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Baptornithidae

facts.statement: Baptornis is classified within the family Baptornithidae.
facts.quote: Family: Baptornithidae

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database classifies Baptornis under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Baptornis is Baptornis advenus.
facts.quote: Type species: Baptornis advenus

facts.statement: Baptornis lived from the Coniacian to the Campanian stages, between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Campanian (89.8 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 10 recorded fossil occurrences of Baptornis in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 10
